Syscall declarations, constants, and helpers for VM logging, runtime, PDA, crypto, and CPI.

# Purpose
`fd_vm_syscall.h` defines the public syscall interface for the VM. It declares the syscall entry points that the VM uses to implement Solana-style runtime services, including logging, memory copy and set operations, sysvar access, return data access, PDA derivation, cross-program invocation, cryptographic hashes, curve operations, and other utility calls. The file also defines constants that control syscall limits and data sizes, such as `FD_VM_RETURN_DATA_MAX`, `FD_VM_PDA_SEEDS_MAX`, and several curve-related size and mode values.

The header also documents the calling rules and return behavior for each syscall. It explains how the VM state is seen at syscall entry, how compute units are charged, and how errors are reported. In addition to syscall prototypes created with `FD_VM_SYSCALL_DECL`, it declares helper functions used by syscall code, such as [`fd_vm_prepare_instruction`](<#fd_vm_prepare_instruction>), [`fd_vm_derive_pda`](<#fd_vm_derive_pda>), and [`fd_vm_translate_and_check_program_address_inputs`](<#fd_vm_translate_and_check_program_address_inputs>). This file is therefore the main declaration point for VM syscall support and related helper APIs.
